observations: Torah #99 (LM2) consists of only three sentences and contains no explicit bechina equations. The text does not use the structural formulas ('X הוא בחינת Y', 'X נקרא Y', etc.) that generate bechina edges. While the Torah touches on several meaningful concepts — הִתְבּוֹדְדוּת (hitbodedut/seclusion), שִׂיחָה בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין קוֹנוֹ (speaking to one's Maker), תְּפִלָּה (prayer as cited from Taanit 8a), נֶפֶשׁ בְּכַפּוֹ (placing one's soul in one's palm), and the emotional states of צַעַר / גַּעְגּוּעַ / כִּסּוּפִים (sorrow, longing, desire) — none of these are connected to each other through bechina language. The Talmudic citation equating the hitbodedut state with 'placing one's soul in one's palm' is stated with 'הַיְנוּ כַּנַּ
